summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of liver transplantation for cryptogenic cirrhosis was readmitted with elevated creatinine and new-onset fever. He had recently completed a course of oral antibiotics for cholangitis but admitted to stopping early due to nausea. He developed fever and confusion, prompting concern for recurrent cholangitis. Imaging showed stable bile duct dilation and a slightly migrated biliary stent, which was repositioned during ERCP. IV antibiotics were administered for a 10-day course, after which fevers resolved and renal function improved. An MRI of the lumbar spine revealed degenerative changes with nerve root impingement but no infection. He was treated for presumed candidal esophagitis, though biopsy was negative. His condition stabilized, and he was discharged home with plans for stent removal in five months and outpatient spine evaluation.
